title: Client Departure Routine
summary: How to close the visit so the client leaves feeling valued, complete, and welcome to return.
relevance: The Client Departure Routine is the final stage of the Zura Spa experience, and it is just as important as the reception and treatment itself.

A client may enjoy an excellent massage, but the way the experience ends can significantly influence how they remember the entire visit. The departure should therefore feel intentional, warm, organised, appreciative, and complete.
The final message should be: "We were happy to have you, your experience mattered to us, and we would genuinely love to welcome you again."

guidelines.title: For the spa, a strong departure routine
list: Reinforces the quality of the service received.
Creates another opportunity to identify whether the client was satisfied.
Helps resolve concerns before the client leaves.
Increases the likelihood of referrals and positive recommendations.
Strengthens the client's emotional connection to Zura Spa.

guidelines.title: For the client
paragraphs: It communicates that they were valued beyond the payment they made. They should feel that the team genuinely cared about how they experienced the service from arrival to departure.

guidelines.title: Appearance
paragraphs: The staff receiving the client after the session must remain properly presented.
The standard at departure should be just as polished as the standard at arrival.
list: Receptionist or therapist should not appear disorganised after the session.
Personal belongings, food, phones, or unrelated items should not be visible around the reception area.

guidelines.title: Attitude
paragraphs: The client should be received with warmth, genuine interest, patience, gratitude, attentiveness, and positive energy.
Never behave as though the important part of the interaction ended once the massage was completed.
The client should not feel that the team is now trying to quickly clear the space for the next customer.

guidelines.title: Disposition
paragraphs: Be cheerful, gracious, professional, calm, appreciative, and engaged.
Make the client feel celebrated rather than processed.
Use the client's name naturally where appropriate and maintain pleasant eye contact.

guidelines.title: Reception Area Arrangement
paragraphs: Before the client returns to reception, the area should already be prepared to receive them.
The client should not return from a relaxing session into a visibly chaotic environment.
list: Free from used cups, food, packaging, or staff belongings.
Free from loud conversations or unnecessary noise.
Properly arranged for any remaining payment or documentation.

guidelines.title: Where required, have these ready
list: Receipt book or digital receipt system.
Any client belongings kept at reception.

guidelines.title: Preparation Before the Client Reaches Reception
paragraphs: The departure routine should begin before the client appears at the front desk. As soon as the therapist indicates that the session is ending:

guidelines.title: 1. Prepare the Reception Area
paragraphs: Straighten the reception area immediately if necessary. Do not wait until the client is already approaching.

guidelines.title: 2. Confirm Any Outstanding Charges
paragraphs: Discreetly confirm with the therapist whether any additional service was provided, the session was extended, any approved add-on was requested, or any outstanding balance remains.
The receptionist should already know this before discussing payment with the client.

guidelines.title: 3. Confirm Tip Arrangement Where Applicable
paragraphs: Where the client has indicated an intention to tip through reception, confirm the arrangement discreetly with the therapist.
Never assume a client intends to tip. Never pressure the client to tip.

guidelines.title: 4. Confirm Complimentary Car Wash
paragraphs: If complimentary car washing applies, confirm with the responsible staff that the vehicle has actually been washed.
Do not announce the complimentary gesture until completion has been verified.

guidelines.title: 5. Be Ready Before the Client Appears
paragraphs: Return to your post and be standing or ready to stand immediately, composed, smiling, and attentive.
The client should not have to arrive at reception and wait for staff to finish a conversation, locate a device, or return from another part of the spa.

procedure.title: Stand and receive the client
procedure.body: As the client approaches reception, stand to acknowledge them. Make pleasant eye contact and receive them warmly. Do not remain seated, distracted, or focused on your phone.

procedure.title: Ask about the client's experience
procedure.body: Invite the client to share how they feel after the session. Use an open question rather than a question that encourages a simple yes/no answer. The question should sound genuinely interested rather than rehearsed.
examples: How are you feeling after your session?
We hope you had a relaxing experience. How was everything for you?

procedure.title: Listen to the response
procedure.body: Do not ask for feedback and then immediately move to payment or another task. Listen. If the client gives positive feedback, thank them, acknowledge it warmly, and share the feedback with the therapist where appropriate. If the client raises a concern, do not become defensive, do not argue, allow them to explain, thank them for bringing it to your attention, and escalate appropriately if necessary. Where possible, the client should leave feeling that their concern was taken seriously.
examples: We're very happy to hear that. Thank you.

procedure.title: Handle outstanding payments
procedure.body: Where there is an outstanding payment for additional services, session extension, approved extras, or other legitimate charges, inform the client politely and clearly. Keep the interaction discreet. Avoid announcing payment details loudly in front of other clients or staff. Payment should feel professional and organised, not confrontational.
examples: Sir, there was an additional 30-minute extension to your session. The additional amount is ₦____.

procedure.title: Handle tips professionally
procedure.body: Where the client has requested to give a tip through reception, receive it professionally, confirm the amount where necessary, ensure it is recorded according to spa procedure, and ensure it reaches the appropriate therapist or account. A tip is an expression of appreciation, not an obligation. Never ask directly whether the client wants to tip, suggest an amount, make the client feel guilty for not tipping, or allow staff to hover around the client expecting a tip.

procedure.title: Mention the complimentary car wash
procedure.body: If the client arrived with a vehicle and the wash has been confirmed, inform them warmly. The purpose is to create an additional positive moment at the end of the experience. Only mention what has been confirmed. Do not say "Your car should have been washed" or "I think they washed your car."
examples: We also had your car washed for you as a complimentary gesture. We hope you enjoy the little surprise.

procedure.title: Encourage the relationship, not just the next sale
procedure.body: Where appropriate, invite the client to return without sounding aggressive or sales-driven. If the client expresses interest in booking another session, assist them immediately. Do not force a future booking on a client who is clearly not interested.
examples: We'd be very happy to welcome you again.
Whenever you need another moment to relax, we'll be glad to have you.

procedure.title: Return any belongings
procedure.body: If any belongings were kept at reception, return them carefully. Ensure everything belonging to the client has been returned before they leave.
examples: Sir, here is your phone and your car key.

procedure.title: Give an intentional farewell
procedure.body: The final goodbye should never feel casual or automatic. Use the client's name where appropriate.
examples: Thank you very much for choosing Zura Spa. It was a pleasure having you today.
We're glad you spent some time with us today. We hope to welcome you again soon.
Thank you for coming. Have a safe journey home, and we look forward to seeing you again.

procedure.title: Acknowledge the client until they leave
procedure.body: Do not immediately sit down, turn away, or return to your phone while the client is still walking out. Maintain polite attention until the departure interaction has naturally ended. Where appropriate, open the door or assist with the exit. The client should feel that the welcome they received when entering was matched by the appreciation they received when leaving.

notes.title: Things Not to Do During Client Departure
Do Not Remain Seated
paragraphs: Always acknowledge an approaching client properly.
Remaining seated while casually saying goodbye can make the interaction feel dismissive.

notes.title: Do Not Ask Weak or Dismissive Feedback Questions
paragraphs: These questions can sound as though the staff simply wants confirmation rather than genuine feedback. Use open questions.

notes.title: Do Not Rush the Client
paragraphs: The spa experience ends when the client leaves, not when the massage stops.
list: Turning your attention to the next client prematurely.
Speaking in a manner that suggests they should leave quickly.

notes.title: Do Not Mention Unconfirmed Services
paragraphs: Never tell the client their car was washed, an item is ready, a booking was made, or an extra service was completed unless it has been verified. Incorrect information damages trust.

notes.title: Do Not Discuss Payment Loudly
paragraphs: Money should be handled discreetly. Do not announce amounts across the reception area or discuss the client's spending in front of others.

notes.title: Do Not Pressure the Client for a Tip
paragraphs: Never:
list: Ask why they are not tipping.
Suggest that a therapist expects a tip.
Compare their tip to another client's.

notes.title: Do Not Ask for Positive Feedback Before Knowing Their Experience
paragraphs: Avoid immediately saying "Please give us a five-star review" before first establishing whether the client was genuinely satisfied.
Client satisfaction should come before review solicitation.

notes.title: Do Not Argue With Negative Feedback
paragraphs: If the client says they were unhappy with something, do not respond with statements such as the following. Listen first. A calm response can sometimes recover an experience that might otherwise result in losing the client.
list: The therapist is actually very good.
You should have said something earlier.

notes.title: Do Not Gossip About the Session
paragraphs: Never discuss the following. Client confidentiality continues even after the client leaves.
list: What happened inside the treatment room.

notes.title: Do Not Become Overly Familiar
paragraphs: A client who enjoyed their session may become more relaxed and conversational afterward. Maintain professional boundaries.
list: Personal comments about the client's body or appearance.

notes.title: Do Not Allow Staff Conflict to Be Visible
paragraphs: Protect the atmosphere until the client is completely out of the spa. The client should never leave while hearing:

notes.title: Do Not Let the Client Leave Without Acknowledgement
paragraphs: Even during a busy period, every client deserves an intentional goodbye. A simple but genuine "Thank you for coming. We hope to see you again." is better than allowing the client to leave unnoticed.

notes.title: The Zura Spa Departure Standard
paragraphs: The ideal departure journey should feel like: Session Completion → Warm Reception → Feedback → Resolution of Outstanding Matters → Added Delight → Appreciation → Farewell.
The departure should reinforce everything the client experienced during the session.
The client should leave thinking: "They cared about my experience." "I was treated properly from beginning to end." "I would like to come back."
notes.closing: The treatment may end in the massage room, but the experience ends at the door. Make the final moments as intentional as the first.
